description.narrative:
Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till GAP för perioden 2016-2018. GAP är en civilsamhällesorganisation som grundades 2007 i Kosovo. GAPs vision är att bygga ett demokratiskt samhälle som garanterar individuell, politisk och ekonomisk frihet for alla dess medlemmar. Organisationen arbetar för att uppnå detta genom två program: 1.) God samhällsstyrning (good governance), inom vilket organisationen bedriver påverkansarbete samt bevakar och informerar om offentliga institutioners arbete och 2.) Utvecklingspolicier, inom vilket GAP bedriver forskning och erbjuder policyrekommendationer för offentliga styrdokument och lagar.
Inom programmet god samhällsstyrning finns ett flertal pågående projekt som berör bland annat bevakning av kommunalpolitik, uppföljning av landets statsbudget, bevakning och publicering av regeringsbeslut, och information om banksektorn. Inom programmet för utvecklingspolicier pågår projekt som berör energisektorn, privatsektorutveckling, effektivitet i statliga företag, samt vägtransport, säkerhet och miljö.

This contribution is a core support to GAP Institute for advanced studies (GAP) 2016-2018. GAP is a non-governmental organisation, established in Kosovo in 2007. GAP's vision is to build a democratic society that guarantees individual, political and economic freedom for all its members. In order to reach this vision the organisation works with two programmes: 1.) Good governance, which includes advocacy and monitoring of public institutions, and 2.) Development Policies, which includes policy research and recommendations pertaining to public policies and laws.
Within the programme for Good governance there are a number of on-going projects covering amongst others: monitoring municipalities; scrutinising the state budget; monitoring and communicating on governmental decisions; and, comparisons and information regarding the banking sector. Within the programme for Development Policies there are currently projects in the following areas: the energy sector, private sector development, effectiveness of public enterprises and car/road traffic policies.

This intervention is in the form of core support and consequently does not have a specific intended outcome. GAP's overall objectives are to bridge the gap between the governance and citizens and between problems and solutions for the advancement of Kosovo society. GAPs key objectives for the period 2016-2018 are to:
1.Further organizational growth; to increase the level of policy documents; to expand the research scope; to strengthen its human resources; and to widen the advocacy activities.
2.Contribute to evidence-based public policies, by providing evidence-based policy recommendations to decision makers, first and foremost to those parliamentary committees whose scope of work falls under GAP's expertise, as well as with other public institutions responsible for economic development and social welfare.
3.Enhance road transport policies, by pressing for a change of government's policies in terms of; used cars not based on age but on Euro standards; substantial improvements in technical control of car safety and emission standards; and a full implementation of the Strategy on Air Quality.
4.Contribute to a competitive private sector, by providing research on fiscal policies, industrial policies, financial incentives and the overall environment of doing business.
5. Maintain a high media presence. Last year GAP Institute was cited 753 times only by online news media. Media in Kosovo plays a major role in creating opinions and advocating for new policies. Therefore, one of GAP's objectives will be maintaining the same level of presence in the media.

description.narrative:
GAP has continuously been one of the most trusted think tanks in Kosovo, delivering reports and inviting for dialogue on different political issues. This Conclusion on Performance, CoP, is being written after two years of cooperation, since the last CoP was replaced by a mayor amendment to the contribution, in December 2022.
Results linked to the role of GAP
The main objective of the work GAP does is to play a crucial role in bridging the gap between the governance and citizens by presenting facts and different perspectives regarding problems and solutions. In doing so GAP undertakes policy relevant research. GAP monitors the work of public institutions, advocates for good governance, and provides concrete recommendations on public policy. By producing reports on current political relevant areas facts and figures are presented in a communicative clear way, which is being used by different stakeholders. GAP also participates in, and sometimes arranges, round-table discussions and debates which makes GAP not only a think tank or research institute, but also a platform for sharing problems and solutions. All of this is linked to the specific goals and thematic areas mentioned above, with room for new topic to dig into.
Sida has since 2016 given GAP a core support to the institution in order for the organization to act freely and choose the relevant topics that also are interesting for the Swedish reform cooperation with Kosovo, and for the strategy goals. The core support has also given room for the staff at GAP to improve their competences and specialist areas.
During the annual meeting on January 26, 2024, GAP stressed (as during previous meetings) that the core support has been crucial for the institution to work adaptively and flexible, following the trends in the society and analyzing what areas are of greatest interest for research and for highlighting statistics that are not shown in other sources.
Sida assesses that this has been of great importance. The support has contributed to GAP's strong role as a think tank and research institute and at the same time as a watch dog in the Kosovo society.
As expressed by the management in GAP, the institution is a leader of monitoring and recommending strategies to strengthen local governance in Kosovo. One example - and result - regarding this is the online platform on mayors electoral promises served as a valuable resource for citizens, media, and policymakers and GAP's following up on the promises.
Another example is how GAP seeks to find improvements when it comes to gender equality. Gender equality remains a pressing issue and GAP has looked at the Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB) at the local level and analyzed how municipalities integrate this issue into their budget planning and execution for a fair distribution of funds. The answer is that a lot remains to do when it comes to improving budget planning and GAP has mentioned recommendations. For instance GAP suggested that Gender-responsive Budgeting and all information regarding GRB should be an integral part of the Draft Budget that is sent for approval in the Assembly of Kosovo, and of the draft budgets.
Sida consider the results of this research very valuable, and that the findings can also be used in other Sida-supported programs - not the least in the upcoming longer program within the agency-to-agency cooperation between the gender equality agencies in Sweden and Kosovo.
GAP has since a few years developed its role thanks to the relation with other think tanks in the Western Balkan, and been active in the regional network WebEcon with six other economic think tanks. During 2023 they had a joint project with the aim to generate evidence and policy dialogue for the food and energy insecurities in the Western Balkan economies pertinent to four key fronts; household livelihoods, firms competitiveness, fiscal space and the regional integration. Sida assesses the joint efforts with other actors in the region can enhance the organization's long term commitments. The institution may also find inspiration and support thanks to the colleague in the region.
During the last two years GAPs staff has continued to develop their professional skills by participating in different workshops and trainings such as in econometrics, workshops to regional countries on public enterprises, and public procurement, tools for support from EU and a like. This was part of the planning and budget with Sida, which now has been fulfilled. By improving the competences within the staff the organization has strengthened the profile and maintained the position as trusted source when it comes to new statistics and analysis.
